episodes.169596: As a backdoor cold front moved into eastern New Mexico, it replinished moisture and provided favorable upslope to allow for more rigorous thunderstorms on July 11, 2022. Thunderstorms developed early in the day and became widespread across much of the northern and central New Mexico. Heavy rainfall was common with these thunderstorms, especially across the northeast due to the boundary. Flash flooding once again impacted the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar. Flash flooding also impacted Highway 56 near Springer. Meanwhile, a few of these thunderstorms became severe with strong winds measured in both Clayton and Fort Sumner.
episodes.169735: Isolated thunderstorms developed across northeast Illinois during the afternoon of July 11th.  One small supercell thunderstorm produced a funnel cloud and isolated wind damage.
episodes.169919: A shortwave trough combined with daytime heating to produce isolated thunderstorms across east-central Wisconsin during the late afternoon and early evening hours on Monday (7/11).  The strongest storm produced wind damage over Manitowoc County before moving offshore.
episodes.169959: Isolated afternoon thunderstorms that developed along the sea breeze produced strong wind gusts as they moved over Brevard County.
episodes.170102: A severe thunderstorm produced strong downburst winds.
episodes.170120: A surface trough moved across the area Monday afternoon, July 11th. Ample wind shear of 30-40 knots, combined with 1500 J/kg of CAPE, caused a few storms to develop across west central Wisconsin. Some hail and gust winds occurred with the strongest storms, one of which caused a wind gust of 67 mph at the KEAU airport.
episodes.170892: A complex of thunderstorms passed across Montana on the evening of July 10th and sent outflow winds many miles southward. High winds occurred at both the Johnson County Airport near Buffalo and the South Big Horn County Airport near Greybull.
episodes.170923: A few thunderstorms across the southeast portions of the state produced some damaging winds and quarter size hail.
episodes.170924: An isolated thunderstorm northwest of Sheridan produced a severe wind gust.
episodes.170966: A line of thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front approaching western Lake Superior during the morning hours of the 11th. While the storms were generally non-severe, a gust to 38 knots was reported at the Duluth Sky Harbor Airport as the storms moved through.
episodes.170971: Isolated thunderstorms produced strong winds over the Lake Michigan waters during the late afternoon and early evening hours on Monday (7/11).
episodes.171091: Storms developed along a cold front located across eastern Nebraska resulting in widespread 70 to 80 mph wind gusts.
episodes.171093: Storms developed along a cold front located western Iowa resulting in widespread 70 to 80 mph wind gusts.
episodes.171341: Isolated damaging wind gusts from thunderstorms and heat bursts occurred during the late evening of Sunday the 10th into the early morning hours of Monday the 11th across limited portions of South Central Nebraska. Scattered thunderstorms developed behind a cold front during the evening hours of July 10th over central and southwestern Nebraska and moved northeast into Valley County between 11PM CDT and midnight. The majority of this activity remained sub-severe, however, the ASOS at Ord Airport measured a marginally-severe wind gust shortly before midnight. This cluster of storms maintained strong to marginally severe intensity as it continued east-northeast through Greeley County. An NeRAIN observer near Spalding noted that strong winds from thunderstorms caused tree and crop damage in the area. An additional Severe Thunderstorm Warning was issued for the same activity in northern Nance County, but no reports were received in this area before convection departed into eastern Nebraska. ||Weak and decaying thunderstorms persisted through the early morning hours of the 11th. With this decaying convection came isolated heat bursts in York County around 4:30AM CDT that produced measured wind gusts near 65 MPH. Another NeRAIN observer noted overturned pivots a few miles east of Waco due to strong winds from these heat bursts.
episodes.171481: A long-lived line of severe thunderstorms clipped far northern Crook County as it moved across the region and produced wind gusts to 60 mph, along with small hail.
episodes.171482: A long-lived line of severe thunderstorms tracked from southeastern Montana through portions of northwestern South Dakota. The storms produced wind gusts to 70 mph across a wide area.
episodes.171483: A long-lived severe thunderstorm tracked from northeastern Wyoming through the northern Black Hills and across west central South Dakota, producing large hail and strong wind gusts across these areas.
episodes.171572: Thunderstorms developed along a surface boundary across Nebraska and into western Iowa in the pre-dawn early morning hours of July 11th. The storms had well established cold pools as they moved into Iowa and an area of favorable MUCAPE which helped to sustain the convection. Storms produced over 70 mph in western Iowa, weakening some into central Iowa with sub-severe wind gusts by the time the storms reached eastern Iowa.
episodes.171698: A cluster of thunderstorms moved along the southeast Georgia coast and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.171719: Supercells over southwest Nebraska moved northeast and eventually merged into a bowing segment during the evening and night of July 10, producing severe hail and wind gusts.
episodes.172208: Isolated showers and thunderstorms across the higher terrain pushed into the I-25 corridor in Pueblo and El Paso Counties through early in the evening. A stronger storm did occur in El Paso County, and produced wind gusts up to around 65 mph.
episodes.172210: Strongest thunderstorm development with the heaviest rainfall on this day was focused over and near the higher terrain. Highest rainfall amounts approaching two inches in a short amount of time caused flash flooding and debris flows across multiple burn scars.
episodes.172271: Isolated thunderstorms developed during the day on the 11th on the backside of an area of low pressure over Lake Superior. While most of the storms were neither strong nor severe, one storm over rural northeastern Pine County interacted with a lake breeze boundary off Lake Superior and developed a weak, brief tornado over a portion of the Nemadji State Forest. The tornado was rated EF-1 based on tree damage visible on satellite analysis.
episodes.172289: Thunderstorms produced severe weather isolated to central South Dakota during the early morning hours. The Pierre Regional Airport reported a peak wind gust of 59 mph.
episodes.172359: Moist southwest flow was over northeast Florida with high pressure southeast of the region and a frontal boundary stretched across southeast Georgia. Showers and storms developed along the I-10 corridor and then moved eastward and merged with the pinned Atlantic sea breeze boundary along the I-95 corridor. Strong storms developed along the merger in the late afternoon into early evening and produced locally heavy rain, brief gusty winds from wet downbursts, and frequent lightning. Light steering flow resulted in slow-moving storms causing street flooding in the westside and northside of Jacksonville.
episodes.172465: Thunderstorms moving across east central Iowa on July 11th brought hail and damaging winds to the area.
episodes.172495: A combination of weak steering flow and tropical moisture resulted in slow moving thunderstorms with torrential downpours that produced a few instances of flash flooding.
episodes.172496: A combination of weak steering flow and tropical moisture resulted in slow moving thunderstorms with torrential downpours that produced a few instances of flooding.
episodes.172780: Strong thunderstorms developed through the afternoon and early evening hours and produced gusty winds that cause minor damage in southwest Alabama.
episodes.172788: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced gusty winds.
episodes.172790: Nickel to quarter sized hail was produced by an isolated storm that moved across portions of Pennington County during the early evening.
episodes.172949: An upper level trough interacted with deep moisture over South Florida to help produce scattered heavy showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.172968: Waterspouts developed in association with a convective cloud line that formed within weak southwest to west lower tropospheric flow.
episodes.172980: Upslope flow combined with a very moist airmass caused training thunderstorms to form along the Alaska Range. The rainfall associated with these thunderstorms caused significant rises to small creeks draining the Alaska Range.

events.narrative: Over 3 inches of rain caused significant rises in creeks draining the Alaska Range from the evening of July 10th. This caused minor damage to several bridges, specifically the ones over Boulder Creek, Lower Suzy Q Creek, Upper Suzy Q Creek, Falls Creek, Gunnysack Creek, and Darling Creek. The Bridge over Bear Creek received significant damage, the approach road being washed out completely. The Richardson highway was closed between MP 281 and MP 234 for over 48 hours. Flooding also damaged a fiber optic cable which resulted in communications disruptions across the Interior.
